newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ says big four bank mergers unlikely.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says big four bank mergers unlikely.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd chief executive Don Mercer said on Wednesday that the high cost of major Australian banks prevented possible takeovers.
"The cost of any of the major Australian banks is so high that I can't see who is going to want to make the acquisition," Mercer told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.

"I think on commercial grounds a takeover is unlikely and certainly on non-takeover grounds -- the sort of friendly merger idea -- I don't think that any of the major Australian banks are of a mind that way," Mercer said.

The Wallis inquiry into the financial sector recommended earlier this month that the "six pillars" policy, which prevented mergers among the four biggest banks and two largest life companies, should be removed.
Treasurer Peter Costello said the government had decided to end the "six pillars" policy, but ruled out mergers between the big four banks at present.
Costello said this would be reviewed when the government was satisfied that competition, particularly in small business lending, had increased sufficiently to allow such mergers to be considered.

The big four private banks are National Australia Bank Ltd , Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac Banking Corp, and ANZ. The latter three banks have a market capitalisation of more than A$12 billion while NAB is valued at more than A$26 billion.
Mercer said previously that the Wallis recommendations were a sensible and comprehensive approach to maintaining the stability and efficiency of Australia's financial system
He said the majority of the proposals in the report echoed the views in the ANZ's submission to the inquiry.
